notes.title: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind is now playable on Controller!
notes.content:
[h1]Controller support[/h1]

We've been hard at work bringing Controller support to Desktop Dungeons: Rewind. Let's have a quick peek at how controller gameplay works while I prattle some marketing speech:

Navigate your way around the depths with ease using our smart targeting technology! The left stick will automatically select the most interesting tile in the direction it was pushed. This way you can zoom straight to your target, even if it's on the other side of the map. (The D-pad allows micro-adjustments for the true exploration connoisseur)

While you fight, you'll want to be using your items and Glyphs. You can go into your inventory to use items, OR you can also use the Radial Menu to sling spells and quaff potions faster than ever!

This all works on the Steam Deck as well, but we're still working towards verification.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/25777715151f22c800738771a45414c190cc0cd9.gif[/img]

Now isn't that fantastic. [i]On to the next big feature...[/i]

[h1]The Codex[/h1]

The Codex is back! Rejoice, revel, write about how glad you are in the Steam Discussions! All of the information you could ever need is at your fingertips. Entries are added when you find something new in a dungeon (including Dailies) or unlock a new Class / Kin.

Information about Gods is also accessible from their altar (no need to alt tab to the wiki anymore!) You'll still need to discover their likes, dislikes, and punishments through experiencing them. So you'll have your inventory deleted at least once :bleaty:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/f9575190dee60bf68dc803df42d714c3e142b187.gif[/img]

[h1]Spanish Localisation[/h1]

Thanks to the amazingly attractive and intelligent members of our Discord server, Azran and Agus, Desktop Dungeons: Rewind now is now playable in Spanish. Grande! They've done a fantastic job and we are so excited to put their hard work into the game 💖 Muchas gracias!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/2e03fa4d14ba74753231d6d241ba9b936dd9a39f.gif[/img]

[h1]Difficulty Modifier[/h1]

Desktop Dungeons: Rewind has a reputation for being difficult, and we don't want this to be something that scares people off. We've added a modifier that should ease players into the game and allow them to experience the terror of later dungeons without sinking hundreds of hours into the game. You can find it in the Gameplay settings.

For the people who like it when the game is difficult, we've added a new feature to the Vicious Token: winning a run with the Vicious Token will raise the Difficulty Modifier by 10%. This can exceed 100%.

We're a little scared to see how far you can take this. :bleaty:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/a1f3fe9fb99ee5782b0444c636126a27453c86f6.gif[/img]

That's all we've got for you today! Enjoy the update, tell your friends, leave a review, follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/QCFdesign]Twitter[/url], join our [url=https://discord.gg/nECGwFe7Y6]Discord[/url], and call your grandma.

Lots of love,
- QCF Design

notes.title: The Goatperson - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #14
notes.content:
[i]“Who is the Goatperson? For the hungry, they are water. For the sick, they are a broken kettle. For the sad, they are a kick to the shin. For the poor, they are late stage capitalism. For the debtor, they are a well aimed blunt instrument to the knee.”[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/b8858dec465752118a2b17961a542456fabf7737.png[/img]

My time has come. Today is the day I write about… the Goatperson. The Goatperson was a sick joke for people who complained that the game was “not roguelike enough,” and a way to thank everyone who supported the game during development (we say thanks in strange ways.)

And now I’m going to “explain” how to play this beautiful abomination of a class. Here’s a GIF showing what it feels like to play Goatperson:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/8bcaa2b70dc13bc1ddb8037a92771ef64562e749.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Abilities[/b][/h2]

🐐 [b]Scapegoat [/b]- Randomly worships a new god per level, no conversion or desecration

🐐 [b]Prototype [/b]- No restoration effects on level-up, gold instead of trophies

🐐 [b]Herbivore [/b]- Eats food while exploring. Killing enemies yields more food

So let’s sum it up: you can die of starvation, have no choice in which God you worship, and don’t heal when you level up. Great. 

[b]Scapegoat [/b]is by far the strangest trait in the game. Starting a run,[b] you’ll automatically be worshipping a God[/b] and their altar will be revealed on the map. You won’t get any piety for the initial worship, and will not gain any of the glyphs they'd usually give you. When you level up, [b]your worship will be forcefully changed to another God.[/b] You’ll have 3 gods in total that will be switched between.

Something worth keeping in mind is that Gods can give boons that will make other Gods ruin your run. If Dracul gives you [b]Life Steal through Blood Hunger[/b], you better [b]pray that Glowing Guardian isn’t in your poo[/b]l. Otherwise, well, uh… BG I guess.

[b]Prototype [/b]hampers you immensely, forcing you to reveal tiles or quaff potions to heal up. Bye bye, well timed level ups! To somewhat make up for this, [b]your conversion bonus is a full health and mana restore[/b]… Except it costs 100 conversion points which increases by 10 every time you use it. Oh, did I mention that it [b]doesn’t cure mana burn and poison like levelling up does[/b]? Yeah, you’ll need potions or a divine intervention to help you with that. 

[b]Herbivore [/b]is just here to make your life even more difficult. Whenever you reveal a new tile, you’ll heal up as per usual and eat one goat food. However, [b]if you don’t have goat food you’ll take damage and drain mana instead.[/b] You start with 90 goat food, and gain 9 every time you kill an experience-valuable monster. This means using [b]Imawal [/b]is usually a bad idea because you’re petrifying your food. 

[quote]“Eating rocks is not recommended.” 
                - local health care professional.[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/1fce463b17cf9db5f6a9c7d371724b9e3367c1d3.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Prayers for the Goatperson[/b][/h2]

When playing the goat person, there are only 2 things you can do: play as well as you can, and pray. Here are some prayers I would recommend:

🔪 [b]Taurog[/b], grant me the strength and fortitude to slay my foes, for I am meagre.

✨ [b]Mystera[/b], provide me magic, for Burndayraz was in the corner of the map.

🌲 [b]Earthmother[/b], forgive me for consuming monsters, for I am hungry. Bah.

💸 [b]Tikki[/b], thank you for accepting cash, for I have nothing else to offer.

👀 [b]Jehora[/b], please don’t randomly poison or mana burn me, for I have no potions left.

📜 [b]Glowing Guardian[/b], bestow on me your Prayer Beads to restore my faith, for I have no hope.

🩸 [b]Dracul[/b], I beg that you are by my side when fighting the boss, for I am weak.

🤝 [b]Pactmaker[/b], give me a slight edge in this dungeon, for I am a pillow in a sword fight.

🗿 [b]Binlor[/b], I am a mere pebble, give me the resistance to least be a small rock. Please.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/c5c9d3c34328844843bc40ccb80889282cc7b81e.png[/img]
[i](Thanks to Eable on our Discord for the ideas!)[/i]

[h2][b]Glyphs[/b][/h2]

🐐 [b]Wonafyt [/b]- The Goatperson’s [b]food delivery service of choice[/b]! Wonafyt teleports an enemy next to the player and slows them. It first teleports monsters that are the same level as the player, and then will teleport lower levels when there are none. [b]Use this to make sure you don’t starve[/b]™.

🐐 [b]Pisorf [/b]- How do you b(l)eat two bosses at once? [b]You headbutt them into each other![/b] If you can line them up, use this glyph to damage both bosses at once while converting your other items for [b]refills on your health and mana. [/b]

🐐 [b]Burndayraz [/b]-  As you might have guessed by this point, the Goatperson is more parts prey than predator. You’d also be a lot more scared of your prey if they could[b] throw fireballs at you[/b]. While you have no bonus to damage like other classes, [b]Burndayraz scales linearly with your level and is almost always useful[/b]. It’s worth preparing [b]Flame Magnet[/b] to make sure you can get through the first couple levels.

One other very useful glyph is [b]Bludtupowa[/b]. Bludtopowa costs health to use, reveals tiles, and restores mana. The great thing is that it reveals 3 tiles but only costs one food. This why you can peak into the fog while[b] saving your snacks for later[/b]. As per usual, using what you find is important. [b]Getindare [/b]will eventually save you from getting hit and therefore save food, [b]Halpmeh [/b]can help with using your tiles efficiently, and [b]Weytwut [/b]can get you out of tight spots.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/2a3ff075fb4f833279b9b5d42d6c0a69d3ea0ed8.png[/img]

The Goatperson actually has some awesome lore behind them, and existed before any other Kin! If you join our Discord and ask, we have a local lore fanatic who'll gladly tell you about it ːbleatyː

Otherwise, that's all we have for today! Here are some chilled goats to make your day.

Follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/QCFdesign]Twitter [/url]and join our [url=https://discord.gg/NKBrHhRxwz]Discord[/url]! See you there, Administrator...

notes.title: The Transmuter - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #13
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/04d120fc2acdd6060f434e9dbf8c0b5fc7e8b7e1.png[/img]

[i]“Transmuters are members of the ancient and powerful Order of Change. Their mastery of inner force is a complete mystery to other magic users: they channel their power through glyphs, yet seem to do so without any techniques outlined in the Standard Magical Primer.”[/i]

Greetings Administrator, and welcome back to another class post! Today we’ll be giving you the basics on how to play the Transmuter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/420cafaf792b00e97ffc3b48f9a2b7add9d3b4a0.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Abilities[/b][/h2]
🌟 [b]Dungeons Lore[/b] -  Starts with a Lemmisi glyph

🌟 [b]Inner Focus[/b] - Using glyphs gives free conversion points

🌟 [b]Spirit Sword[/b] - Hitting the conversion threshold adds temporary damage based on max mana

Before explaining the Transmuter’s abilities, let's lay some groundwork. [b]Conversion [/b]is the ability of all adventurers to turn items and glyphs into [b]power[/b]. This power [b]depends on their Kin[/b]. When converted, an item will give you a number of [b]Conversion Points[/b] specified in its description. Once your Conversion Points reach your [b]conversion threshold[/b], you’ll gain the bonus and start working towards the next threshold. 

Transmuters are the masters of conversion. [b]Inner Focus[/b] provides you with conversion points [b]equal to your mana spent[/b] whenever you cast a glyph, and [b]Spirit Sword[/b] gives a massive spike in [b]damage [/b]when you hit a conversion threshold! This makes Transmuters an excellent choice in long dungeons where you’re bound to cast plenty of glyphs and convert plenty of items. 

The base damage given by Spirit Sword is [b]equal to your maximum mana[/b]. This means that finding sources of [b]bonus damage[/b] through your Kin, items, or glyphs can go a long way in making you stronger. Much like the Sorcerer, you’ll have a very diverse damage profile, which can make finding fightable enemies a lot easier.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/39b073d239ed7c128c4e4d17f97e91e065c3b703.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Kin Choices[/b][/h2]
🌟 [b]Human [/b]- Humans gain [b]10% bonus damage[/b] when they reach a conversion threshold. Along with having the best scaling power, this synergises well with [b]Spirit Sword[/b]! Human Transmuters can deal truly monstrous damage, and will shine later in a run.

🌟 [b]Elf [/b]- Elves gain [b]one maximum mana[/b] when they reach their conversion threshold. This obviously synergises with Spirit Sword to give you more damage, but there’s something even better… You have the lowest conversion threshold in the game. You’ll deal more damage, more often, and receive a permanent increase to your mana.

🌟 [b]Dwarf [/b]- Dwarves gain [b]+10 max HP[/b] per 80 conversion points. This is another cheap threshold, and can lead to a Dwarf Transmuter becoming incredibly tanky. In Desktop Dungeons, the amount of damage you can deal is effectively how much [b]health you can afford to trade[/b] without dying. More health, more effective damage. Dwarves become powerful faster than Elves and Humans, but don't scale when enemies start dealing lots of damage.

You’ll be reaching conversion thresholds often as a Transmuter, and so your Kin choice makes more of a difference than most other classes. Below is a table showing each Kin’s conversion bonus and how many conversion points are needed for a threshold. Happy theory crafting! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/ca91533add58580dc3f05a8003b39f79c739cb79.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/02126b860fff49b0cf7c87696865233aabf753f0.png[/img]

[h2][b]Gods[/b][/h2]
🌟 [b]Jehora Jeheyu[/b] - The God of Madness appears again. What is change if not Chaos? Transmuters gain their power from casting spells, which Jehora will [b]reward with Piety[/b]. [b]Boost Mana[/b] will increase your maximum mana and make your [b]Spirit Sword[/b] stronger. If you can save enough piety to become the [b]Chaos Avatar[/b], you’ll be rewarded with 100 Conversion Points, a level-up, and a cure for your ailments.

🌟 [b]Mystera Annur[/b] - Change is made in a struggle for growth. Jehora and Mystera are two sides of the same coin: Mystera rewards you for [b]casting spells[/b], and can boost your maximum mana through [b]Magic[/b]. They also offer mana refills for converting glyphs with [b]Refreshment[/b], and Flames can be picked up if you plan to go full fireball. 

🌟 [b]Glowing Guardian[/b] - Conversion returns you to order. [b]Humility [/b]lowers your level by one without affecting your health or damage, which makes your [b]Spirit Sword[/b] damage spikes effective at catapulting you to [b]higher levels[/b]. Glowing Guardian will also reward you for converting items. This piety can be used to reach [b]Enlightenment [/b]for a boost to maximum mana, damage, health, and conversion points.

Most Gods are useful for the Transmuter. [b]Tikki Tooki [/b]is helpful because you aren’t a regen fighter and they give you a free [b]Getindare [/b]glyph. With [b]Binlor[/b], you can farm piety and conversion points simultaneously with [b]Endiswal[/b]. [b]Knockback[/b] damage also has synergy with Spirit Sword!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/f7b445523fe9886125652d810129c087a0ccac92.png[/img]

[h2][b]Glyphs[/b][/h2]
🌟 [b]Bysseps [/b]- Spirit Sword gives you base damage for one attack, and Bysseps give you [b]bonus damage for one attack[/b]. If you want to power up your swing as much as possible, this is the biggest it’s going to get! This combo is great for taking down higher level enemies to get you some bonus experience.

🌟 [b]Getindare [/b]- As much as we like to believe whoever you’re spiking on will die instantly, sometimes they won’t. Using Getindare in these moments for [b]an extra attack[/b] that converts their existence into… Non-existence. If you're feeling fancy, plan ahead and have the conversion points gained from [b]Inner Focus[/b] push you over the threshold in the middle of combat!

🌟 [b]Lemmisi [/b]- What this Glyph lacks in combat power, it makes up for in [b]utility[/b]. Lemmisi [b]reveals 3 random tiles[/b], and the revealed tiles count towards your regeneration. You’ll heal for three tiles of health and one mana. It also has the special property of [b]prioritising helpful tiles[/b]. Using it as a substitute for exploring to heal can help to reveal useful glyphs, hidden subdungeons, boosters, and God Altars. It will also give you conversion points through [b]Inner Focus[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/2d2800b26553f148f30121ebb4584cb2d19c9fcc.png[/img]

That's all for this post. Remember to be kind, and give your parents a call!

notes.title: The Rogue - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #12
notes.content:
[i]"Rogues are mavericks with a touch of class. Although they inhabit the greyer areas of society, they put themselves above "common" criminals and hone their skills in preparation for all sorts of glory-seeking exploits. Their grace and poise in battle is unmatched. Their durability, unfortunately, is not."[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/99f7459ee04bf903ef7744ba374f7ccf1fd4854d.png[/img]

Welcome back to another Class Post! Sneaking into the fray, today we'll be talking about the Rogue: the epitome of being able to dish it out but not being able to take it. They're a straightforward and versatile class that works around reduced health and quick hits.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/bea77a20de6ab119dad432a1a1217dfbae65bc00.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Abilities[/b][/h2]

🔪 [b]Dangerous [/b]- -5 health per level, but start off with +40% damage

🔪 [b]Dexterous [/b]- Permanent First Strike buff

🔪 [b]Evasive [/b]- Starts with 20% Dodge

[b]Dangerous [/b]is the Rogue’s Defining trait, turning them into the glassiest cannon of Desktop Dungeons: Rewind. +40% base damage is an unrivalled boost to damage, but they gain health [b]at half the rate[/b] of a normal class. This health penalty is sometimes offset by their amazing dexterity.

[b]Dexterous [/b]and [b]Evasive [/b]can put you up by two hits in a fight: one because you might [b]Dodge [/b]their hit, and a second because [b]you have First Strike[/b]. This means that you have [b]2 more attacks[/b] worth of effective HP! There are two risks to this though: your dodge chance is [b]only 20%[/b] which needs to be maximised by taking more hits, and [b]enemies with First Strike will still hit you first[/b]! These can be manoeuvred around, which we’ll get into later.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/269f8a37ab67c7396be39a106e7db7d889d3f396.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Kin choices[/b][/h2]

🔪 [b]Orc [/b]- Leaning into the [b]full glass cannon[/b], Orc Rogues can have truly massive amounts of damage. Their Conversion bonus grants them [b]+2 base damage[/b], which turns into a lot of damage after the Rogue’s [b]40% damage multiplier[/b]. Downside is… You’ll need health from [i]somewhere [/i]otherwise you will likely die if you don’t kill your target in one or two hits. You can find this health in [b]items [/b]or [b]Deities[/b].

🔪 [b]Dwarf [/b]- Taking the safer route, Dwarves get[b] 10 HP[/b] from their Conversion bonus. This allows them to survive up to two to three hits, [b]increasing the chance of a dodge[/b] and still being up an attack from First Strike. You’ll have to find [b]items [/b]to boost your base damage to get the most out of [b]Dangerous [/b]though.

🔪 [b]Goblin [/b]- Orcs and Dwarves are far and away the best Rogues… But an unconventional yet effective choice is the Goblin. Goblins gain [b]experience [/b]from their Conversion bonus, and levelling up gives the player [b]+5 base damage[/b]. This makes the Rogue’s multiplier more valuable, and on top of that, levelling will [b]fully heal you[/b]. Combine this with a [b]Cydtsepp[/b], and watch as the boss takes five massive hits in a row! Who doesn't want to stab people with a pencil?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/e0a601fec9b6743ee28c45e70fe95d1a70aa41f1.png[/img]

[h2][b]Glyphs[/b][/h2]

🔪 [b]Cydstepp [/b]- [b]Death Protection[/b] is amazing on Rogues as it guarantees you'll be able to take one last hit… And with Rogues, every hit counts. Not only this, but it can be cast [b]before a fight[/b] ("precasted") which allows you to regenerate your mana before you fully engage. Combine this with any other combat focused Glyph and you’ll have a [i]killer [/i]time!

🔪 [b]Apheelsik [/b]- With its fairly low cost and ability to [b]stop enemies from regenerating[/b], you can use this Glyph to sneak in another attack without perishing like milk in a Vegan’s fridge. It’s a little worse than Cydstepp because it [b]doesn’t last long on higher level enemies[/b] and [b]isn’t precastable[/b], but still a great pickup.

🔪 [b]Weytwut [/b]- Weytwut inflicts the [b]Slowed [/b]status effect. When slowing an enemy, you’ll get 1 [b]additional experience [/b]for killing them and temporarily [b]remove their First Strike[/b]. Goblins and Gorgons are squishy but have First Strike and lots of damage… Completely negating your First Strike and taking advantage of your reduced HP. Pull out Weytwut to turn the tables in your favour!

All of these Glyphs help you to get an [b]extra attack[/b] in one way or another. Other Glyphs that help with this are [b]Endiswal [/b]for the physical resistances or [b]Halpmeh [/b]for some healing. [b]Burndayraz [/b]can also serve as a finisher or to mitigate some regeneration!

We’ve talked about Glyphs before Gods in this post because the Glyphs you’re using will likely change based on who you’re worshipping.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/a2611d0038a48185689ccc93676d2dcdb39003c2.png[/img]

[h2][b]Gods[/b][/h2]

🔪 [b]Tikki Tooki[/b] - The main downside of Tikki is that they punish you when you get hit a lot. Well guess what, you can’t get hit a lot anyways! Using [b]Reflexes[/b], you can have [b]dodge prediction[/b] from the Quicksilver Potion, and get [b]two attacks[/b] in one swing from the Reflex Potion. [b]Dodging [/b]can further increase your dodge chance and Tikki rewards you for dodging attacks. Just be careful about using [b]Cydstepp[/b], as you’ll be [b]punished [/b]for triggering a Death Protection. That will likely end your run. Use [b]Weytwut [/b]and [b]Apheelsik [/b]instead to get some free piety!

🔪 [b]Glowing Guardian[/b] - Glowing Guardian synergises well with the Rogue on many fronts. [b]Absolution [/b]gives you a beneficial health increase, and the downside of [b]Humility [/b]lowering your regen doesn’t matter as much because of your low health maximum. [b]Cleansing [/b]can turn your massive physical attack into a magical one, and [b]Health Potions[/b] weren’t doing too much for us anyways so it doesn't feel bad to convert them. Just make sure to [b]not use Apheelsik,[/b] as you’ll be heavily punished. Try [b]Cydstepp [/b]or [b]Weytwut [/b]instead!

🔪 [b]Jehora Jeheyu[/b] - The god of Primordial Chaos appears again! [b]Boost Health[/b] is great for the Rogue, as well as giving you a free [b]Weytwut [/b]glyph when you begin worshipping them. Just make sure you have a plan to deal with the small punishments, as a level or two of Weakened can make your run a lot harder. Reaching Chaos Avatar is always a noteworthy spike

Unlike with Kin, Rogues can make great use of many different Deities. [b]Earthmother [/b]gives health with [b]Vine Form[/b] and slows enemies with [b]Entanglement[/b], [b]Binlor [/b]can help you build up some [b]resistances[/b], and [b]Taurog [/b]can be dipped into early for [b]armour [/b]and [b]Skullpicker [/b]before converting out. Even [b]Mystera [/b]can give you some bonus mana and lower the cost of useful spells! 

That’s the entire pantheon, so keep an eye out for cheeky [b]conversions [/b]and play around the Glyphs that you find.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/16deeb9d2af9ea1d16321e598f03021f3392f635.png[/img]

Rogues can tackle the hardest Dungeons your Desktop has to offer and now you know the basics of how to play them! 

If you want to play the Rogue ASAP, buy Desktop Dungeons: Rewind!
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1976950/Desktop_Dungeons_Rewind/

Follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/QCFdesign]Twitter [/url]and join our [url=https://discord.gg/NKBrHhRxwz]Discord[/url]! See you there, Administrator.

notes.title: Every Dungeon and Quest... Explained in one guide!
notes.content:
[h1]Our amazing community has done it again! [/h1]

Laberca, Rewind playtester and veteran Desktop Dungeons player, has compiled every Dungeon and Quest into one guide. Each section contains details about bosses, map mechanics, quests, and strategies to help you complete them. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/ac53e4f20daa32ea3f96283d1a9b1e1e7fa5cb0e.png[/img]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2967962296

As a preview of the guide, here is Laberca's break down of Havendale Bridge:

[h1]Hard Dungeons - Havendale Bridge[/h1]

[h2]Difficulty[/h2]
★★★★★★ (Hard - 105%)

[h2]Enemies[/h2]
Goats, goblins, bandits, and one other common enemy.

[b]Rusalka[/b]:
Attack: 100%
Health: 100%
Corrosive (inflicts 1 stack of corrosion when it hits you, permanently increasing all damage you take by 1 - the stacks are hard to get rid of. Also leaves a corrosive pool instead of a blood pool)

[b]Tokoloshe[/b]:
Attack: 100%
Health: 100%
50% physical resist
Cowardly
Trophy: Tokoloshe charm (small item that grants +5% magic resist)

[b]Druid[/b]:
Attack: 80%
Health: 80%
Death protection
Magical attack

[h2]Bosses[/h2]
One random common boss

[b][i]Bridge Troll[/i][/b]: (Optional level 5 miniboss, but guards the bridge. Can be bypassed by spending 20 gold or with magic)
Attack: 19
Health: 70
Fast regen
Berserks at 50%
50% resists
Trophy: Sensation stone (lockerable item that can be converted for 150 CP)

[b]Zin Kibaru[/b]:
Attack: 78
Health: 415
Magical attack
25% magic resist
Undead
Bloodless

[h2]Gimmicks[/h2]
The dungeon is divided in half by a river, guarded by the Bridge Troll. You can skip the bridge troll by paying it 20 gold.

[h2]Recommended Classes + Races[/h2]
Any can work, but Berserker will utterly trivialize Zin Kibaru, Bloodmage has an easier start than most, and Monk scales well due to the charms.

[h2]Strategy[/h2]
This dungeon has a forgiving difficulty modifier, but the divided map can make the early game a bit tough. For new players, you might want to consider just paying the Troll Toll of 20 gold to get past him.

If you are having a strong early game, it is definitely worth fighting the troll - he gives you 5 XP and an extra 150 CP, plus you won't have to spend 20 gold.

Alternatively, if you find WEYTWUT or PISORF, you can use that to bypass him without spending gold and save him for later, when you are a higher level! This is basically always the ideal approach if you can do it.

The monster set here is pretty varied. Rusalkas are tough for non-casters, as you don't want to get corroded. Tokoloshe's are tough but drop a charm that boosts your magic resist. Druids are very weak and super easy to kill, especially if you have some tokoloshe charms. Look for high level druids!

Zin Kibaru is usually quite easy because of the charms, so usually you want to go after him first.

[h2]Quests[/h2]
[b]Troll Toll[/b]: Defeat Havendale Bridge. (Unlocks the Labyrinth and Magma Mines)
★★★★★★
All you have to do for this quest is win. Just follow the general strategy tips! Probably the most straightforward build here is an Orc Berserker.

[b]Unlikely Heroes[/b]: Forest Edition Win with a Halfling Wizard, Halfling Monk, and Halfling Rogue. (Rewards 500 gold)
★★★★★★★
This is part of the Unlikely Heroes quest line, which forces you to use suboptimal race+class combos.

Fortunately, none of these combos are horrible - they just aren't very good. You don't really need any special strats for these runs. The wizard especially shouldn't be tough. The monk run is harder, but monk is a good class here - just look for some damage bonuses and prep a base damage item if you can. The rogue combo is a little unfortunate because rogue isn't the best class here, but if you just focus on getting your health up with items or gods like Jehora Jeheyu, you shouldn't have much of an issue.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/ff0eb16a02ec26cd489799b7ef32c79bd8701729.png[/img]

And that's all! Make sure to join our [url=https://discord.gg/NKBrHhRxwz]Discord[/url] and thank Laberca yourself if you found this guide helpful.

notes.title: Struggling to fight your way through dangerous dungeons? Read this guide!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/bd29962c7cc18d76073de39e997a908a53233555.png[/img]

Are the goats bleating you death? Or are the meat men mushing your under-leveled and ill-prepared adventurer? With these seven simple tips, you'll be showing them who the boss is! 

[b]Eable2[/b], long time Desktop Dungeons player and Desktop Dungeons: Rewind playtester, has put together an amazing guide to help out anyone who is struggling. Here's a link to the full guide: 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2964276019

While you should read the full guide, here are some snippets of the seven habits:

[h3]#1: Don't fight your equals ❌[/h3]
[list]
[*]Killing higher level enemies gives you bonus experience
[*]Monster that are the same level as you will attack first anyways and not give bonus XP
[*]If you don't punch up, you'll be too weak to fight the boss
[/list]

[h3]#2: Leverage Levels 🔼[/h3]
[list]
[*]Levelling fully restores mana and health, it also cures poison and mana-burn
[*]Levelling up during a boss fight can be incredibly potent
[*]Do this by eating your snacks (see #3)
[/list]

[h3]#3: Save Snacks for Later 🍿[/h3]
[list]
[*]You can kill low level enemies in 1 hit, we call them "popcorn"
[*]Use WONAFYT to make a popcorn bowl and munch for a spike
[*]Some enemies aren't good snacks
[/list]

[h3]#4: Know Your Tools 🔨[/h3]
[list]
[*]Glyphs help immensely with killing higher level enemies
[*]Class Abilities can help you find power in specific situation
[*]Find items that synergise with your strategy
[/list]

[h3]#5: Explore with Intention 🥽[/h3]
[list]
[*]Enemies also regenerate when you explore, so be careful!
[*]Wasting tiles by not regenerating [i]something[/i] is usually a bad play
[*]Sneakily reveal small amounts of tiles while fighting to get kills
[/list]

[h3]#6: Save Your Spikes 💪[/h3]
[list]
[*]Save potions for a major fight, try not to use them on curing status effects (see #2)
[*]This also applies to items that give you a temporary boost
[*]Save your snacks! Patience!
[/list]

[h3]#7: Eyes on the Prize 🏆[/h3]
[list]
[*]Remember, you win by killing the boss. Don't get distracted!
[*]Power up before the boss fight as much as possible by buying new things and converting what you don't need
[/list]

And that's it! Again, massive thanks to Eable for putting this guide together and helping out the fresh blood. If you want to say thanks personally, join our Discord! There are multiple magnificent and seasoned Administrators who are here to help!

notes.title: So... What's different in Rewind?
notes.content:
Hey there! So there have been a couple changes from the original Desktop Dungeons to Desktop Dungeons: Rewind. Over the years, we've become wiser goats and made some adjustments to past choices. Sorry it's a day late, but here's a list of all the design changes we've made!

[h2][b]Kin [/b][/h2]

[h3]Nomenclature[/h3]
[i]"There are better words in the English language, and we want to use them!"[/i]
[quote]Nomenclature: Race >>> Kin[/quote]
[h3]Orc[/h3]
[i]"Orcs were by far the most dominant Kin in Desktop Dungeons, so we're taking them down a notch. They're still good, just not quite as OP."[/i]
[quote]Orc Conversion Threshold: 80 >>> 100[/quote]
[h3]Dwarf[/h3]
[i]"The Dwarf conversion felt a little lacklustre because of its delayed strength, and on top of this they were a little weak. Let's fix both of those, and make them beefy earlier while scaling up to the same point."[/i]
[quote]Dwarf Conversion Bonus: +1 Max HP per level >>> 10 Max HP[/quote]

[h2][b]Classes[/b][/h2]

[h3]Fighter[/h3]
[i]"The Fighter is the first class you unlock, and it teaches you to play the game wrong. The old Fighter encouraged you to seek out and farm low level enemies, starving you of experience late game. The new fighter encourages you to hit higher level enemies, maybe even realise you can kill them for bonus XP!"[/i]
[quote][b]Veteran XP bonus[/b]: +1XP per kill >>> Level difference in XP when first attacked by a higher level enemy
[b]Instincts[/b]: Same and lower enemies revealed >>> Sense enemies 1 tile further into the fog[/quote]
[h3]Transmuter[/h3]
[i]"The idea for Transmuters is awesome: cast spells to gain Conversion Points, and get a massive spike when you hit a Conversion Threshold. Except... Only a small portion of the spells are efficient, and hitting that threshold drained you mana so you can't cast spells. We've moved some of their power around to make them more fun and slightly stronger."[/i]
[quote][b]Spirit Sword[/b]: No longer drains mana on Conversion Threshold
[b]Spirit Sword temporary damage[/b]: Max mana + level >>> Max mana
[b]Inner Focus[/b]: Gives 3 Conversion Points on glyph cast >>> Gives mana cost as Conversion Points on glyph cast
[/quote]
[h3]Berserker[/h3]
[i]"Berserkers could use some more flavour, and now we have a new inventory system... Let's use it! Also, the Goblin Berserker showed their fashion prowess in Berserker Fashion Week, so we gave them a prize. You go, Gobzerker!" [/i]
[quote][b]Inventory size[/b]: 30 >>> 35
Goblin Berserker start with a [b]Golden Spork[/b][/quote]
[h3]Chemist[/h3]
[i]"Who plays Chemist anyways?"[/i]
[quote]Potion resource restore: 10% >>> 20% 
Multiple casts of Bysseps now stacks erosion
[/quote]

[h2][b]Inventory[/b][/h2]

[i]"This is more of a convenience change and fits better with the new UI. It also gives us something to play with (see the Berserker and a new item.)"[/i]
[quote]No longer split into 5 slots, now a total of 30 size
Small items have a size of 1
Large items have a size of 5
[/quote]

[h2][b]Early Game Difficulty[/b][/h2]

[i]"Players found that the difficulty spike when fighting the bankers was too large. We don't want people to be put off by that and so there have been a couple changes to welcome new players. Some are direct (changed early enemy strength) and some are indirect (scouting and predictive combat logs.) Overall, new players should have a better time."
[/i]
[h3]Scouting[/h3]
[i]"This applies to all classes, and should give players a better sense of which direction to explore. Also the looming presence of enemies is fun."[/i]
[quote]All classes will now scout one tile into the fog, showing the presence of enemies and their levels
Enemies with Life-steal will not be revealed in this way
[/quote]
[h3]Rewind Insurance[/h3]
[i]"He said the name of the game. Roll the credits."[/i]
[quote]Defeating the Bankers will grant you Rewind insurance!
Once per run when die for the first time, you’ll have the option to go back to about half way through your run
[/quote]
[h3]Simulated Predictions[/h3]
[i]"One of the biggest changes in Rewind is simulated predictions. In combat your damage may change from being weakened or corroding your enemy. The game now does the maths for you.[/i]
[quote]Combat is now simulated, giving more accurate combat predictions that change based on status effects
God punishments, random events, and some more complicated effects are not simulated
[/quote]
[h3]Banker difficulty[/h3]
[i]"The numbers on this are hard to describe. Just trust us, it's easier than it was."[/i]
[quote]Dungeons leading up to and including the Bankers have been nerfed.[/quote]

[h2][b]Dungeon Generation[/b][/h2]

[i]"The purpose of Desktop Dungeons: Rewind was to bring fresh life into Desktop Dungeons, including better visual compatibility with wide ratio screens. Square dungeons on rectangular screens didn't feel great, so now the shape of Dungeons will adapt to your monitor (this doesn't affect difficulty!)"[/i]
[quote]Dungeons will be 25 x 16 tiles for wide aspect ratio
Dungeons will be 20 x 20 tiles for squarer aspect ratio
[/quote]

[h2][b]Goat Glade[/b][/h2]

"This used to be a part of the DLC that we didn't want to be mandatory for high level play. Now that it's part of the base game, we can make it better!"
[quote][b]Item Lottery[/b]: removed
[b]Item Registry[/b]: After bringing an item to the Goat Glade three times, the goats will be able to make the item as many times as you want at prep cost.

notes.title: The Fighter, Thief, Priest, and Wizard - Exploring character classes #15
notes.content:
Not only is this a double threat class post, it’s a double double threat! (Double threat)^2, if you will. Today is a little different: we’ll be giving a general overview for all of the tier 1 classes, and talk tips on how to play them. We’ll also be giving hints for their class challenges, as they’re a load of fun and unlock items for your normal runs. We’ll be finishing off with some other basic tips for advancement if you get stuck. Let’s get into it!

[h2][b]Fighter[/b][/h2]
[h3]Abilities[/h3]
💪 [b]Instincts [/b]- Can sense enemies farther away in the fog
💪 [b]Veteran [/b]- Gains XP when attacked by higher level enemies, and less XP needed per level
💪 [b]Pit Dog[/b] - Dungeons runs start with 1 level of standard Death Protection on the character.

Don’t let the name deceive you, Fighters are very versatile. They make great use of spells and while also being fantastic strikers. Poke higher level enemies for XP, maybe realise you can actually kill them! You’ll be able to level up and get stronger, faster. Better. Harder.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/bd74c538049696ec7245473851e1a6230b750249.gif[/img]

[h3]Kin[/h3]
💪 [b]Dwarf [/b]- Dwarves were buffed in Rewind, and they’re great if you want a forgiving experience in early dungeons. +10 max HP can help you roll the early levels, so get a conversion in early.
💪 [b]Goblin [/b]- Fighters are good at levelling up, Goblins are good at giving experience. What a match. While you won’t have any combat bonus from conversion, using level ups as heals is great, so keep an eye out for them!
💪 [b]Elf [/b]- As we’ve said, fighters are not just focused on hitting things and can use spells well. Burndayraz’s damage scales with level, and Elves can help you get more casts off! There’s an early quest that’ll have you playing this way, so you’ll see the strength.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/a635277f3096ea2ac8f210d65460d7ecde3efe5e.png[/img]

[h3]Class challenges[/h3]
The first fighter challenge is fairly simple: use Wonafyt and Imawal to get enough levels and then take on the boss. Using Imawal on an enemy that is slowed from Wonafyt will give you one bonus XP, and the next enemy you kill after using Imawal will grant 50% more XP.

💪 Use all of your mana before exploring
💪 Use Imawal on slowed enemies for more XP
💪 Convert your items before fighting the boss for an extra edge

The second challenge is a little harder because you’ll be dealing with Goo Blobs, which have high physical resistance. Kill them with Burndayraz when you find it, and make sure to get value out of Veteran XP. The boss deals tons of damage, and attacks back when you Burndayraz. Potions are your friend!

💪 Get Veteran XP value from enemies you can’t kill
💪 Pay attention to your glyphs and where you can use them
💪 The boss will require many health and mana potions to beat

[h2][b]Thief[/b][/h2]
[h3]Abilities[/h3]
🔪 [b]Stabber [/b]- Deals an extra 30% damage to enemies with full health
🔪 [b]Hoarder [/b]- +33% more items on dungeon map
🔪 [b]Survivor [/b]- All Health Potions and Mana Potions restore both health AND mana

You scale incredibly well with Stabber and can spike super hard for a boss fight with potions! Make sure you hit enemies before you Burndayraz them to not lose your bonus damage from Stabber. This class gets better as you unlock items, so do the class challenges!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/45d1b0afa12a7a5af761b67076d668853b6198d6.gif[/img]

[h3]Kin[/h3]
🔪 [b]Halfling [/b]- Having more health potions for synergy with Survivor is super strong. This will focus more around attacking
🔪 [b]Gnome [/b]- Much like the halfling, more potions gives more value from Survivor. However, you’ll be more focussed on spells like Pisorf and Burndayraz.
🔪 [b]Orc [/b]- Gaining base damage from their conversion bonus, Orcs focus more on getting value out of Stabber. Glyphs like Getindare and Bysseps will be super useful.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/b3f048dd1ce1112d97de9bf56d510a09fe815092.png[/img]

[h3]Class challenges[/h3]
This class has the strangest and most difficult challenges. In the bronze challenge, you’ll be playing around Getindare to take out bandits, collect their charms for health and damage, and then take out Trapped chests for their loot. The chests hit hard, so make sure you can regen enough!

🔪 An enemy with First strike will always hit you first, unless it is slowed
🔪 You’ll always be level 1 in this challenge, so your HP regen will be very slow
🔪 Take out the trapped chests ASAP! The 5th one will help you with the final boss

The silver challenge is ROUGH, but it will teach you how to use Lemmisi and Weytwut effectively. You’ll find the trapped chests again, but the enemies are far stronger. Use Lemmisi to reveal more tiles, and Weytwut to swap positions with revealed enemies.

🔪 Weytwut can be used on enemies that are far away
🔪 Lemmisi will always restore 1 mana when cast, use it to get out of sticky situations
🔪 While you’ll need potions for the final boss, using them to level up is also a good choice

[h2][b]Priest[/b][/h2]
[h3]Abilities[/h3]
💒 [b]Good Health[/b] - An extra 3 health is gained per level
💒 [b]Good Drink[/b] - Health Potions are 100% effective
💒 [b]Good Golly[/b] - Physical damage against Undead is +100%

Good Health and Good Drink alone make this class super strong. Every potion is a full health restore, and you have massive amounts of health. This combined with picking off high level undead enemies (vampires and zombies preferably) can turn you into a powerhouse.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/ecf75644ef1272bf7e011c34976bb7c9874127ce.gif[/img]

[h3]Kin[/h3]

💒 [b]Halfling[/b] - More health potions to make use of Good Drink is a monstrously strong combo for taking down bosses, particularly in the Eastern Tundra
💒 [b]Orc [/b]- Increased base damage will help you to kill some high level undead early, and scale up into some crazy damage late game
💒 [b]Elf [/b]- This is more of a fun choice that ends up being a strong and balanced experience. You’ll be slinging spells more than other Priests, so enemies with high physical resists don’t get you down.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/d316869d858f86a74682ac31b2875340ed7ed447.png[/img]

[h3]Class challenges[/h3]

This class has the most simple challenges to complete, but the second challenge will be locked behind finding Gods (don’t worry, you’ll run into them.) The bronze challenge is fairly simple: kill undead, and find a chainsaw and shotgun to help you out. I’m not joking.

💒 Look for kills on higher level undead to boost your levelling
💒 Find tools to help you get that job done

The silver challenge is similar to the bronze challenge, except you won’t have as many undead enemies to pick off and Goo Blobs will have physical resistances. The boss is also incredibly tough, so make sure to save all of your health potions.

💒 Burndayraz and regen fighting Goo Blobs is the best way to take them down
💒 Save health potions and a level-up for the final boss. Frank has an unreasonable amount of health and damage.

[h2][b]Wizard[/b][/h2]
Wizard is fun if you like slinging some spells, and they work well with 2 other kin that have mana synergy (Gnome and Elf). And for my money Sorcerer is one of the most enjoyable classes in the game, so getting them early is fun!

[h3]Abilities[/h3]
🧙‍♂️ [b]Magic Sense[/b] - Can see locations of all glyphs from level start, all glyphs are small items.
🧙‍♂️ [b]Magic Affinity[/b] - Skills cost -1 mana, glyphs donate 10 points to other conversions.
🧙‍♂️ [b]Magic Attunement[/b] - Starts with Burndayraz, double burning stacks

See those little blue marks in the fog? Those are Glyphs! Make your way towards them to get value from Magic Affinity value ASAP. You don’t need to worry about holding them and clogging your inventory because they’re small. Magic Affinity will give you 2 Burndayraz casts from level 1, but the second part needs some explanation: holding more glyphs makes your conversions better. This means you can hoard Glyphs and convert bought items for massive amounts of conversion points. This makes your choice of Kin important.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/c99552abc89f606af3f23fe7d4699fa52ee8b282.gif[/img]

[h3]Kin[/h3]
🧙‍♂️ [b]Gnome [/b]- Mana Potions are great for spiking against bosses in a way that having more mana sometimes can’t match. Having more mana potions can also make getting Mana burned less of an issue.
🧙‍♂️ [b]Elf [/b]- Don’t get me wrong: having more max mana can help your early game tremendously, and it comes at a super low conversion cost. However, once you reach a point where it takes 18 tiles to fill your mana bar, things can get awkward. Still strong though!
🧙‍♂️ [b]Orc[/b] - Do you know of Punchomancy? It’s not a tale the Wizards would tell you. The Orc’s conversion bonus is +2 base damage… Pisorf’s damage scales with your base damage and costs less mana than Burndayraz. Not to mention having more base damage great for synergy with Getindare and Bysseps. Go get em’ and be the best Punchomancer around.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/822ed73162bcff6f7df64b02353c05fbdd93580c.png[/img]

[h3]Class challenges [/h3]
The bronze wizard challenge is very easy as long as you read your spells. The guards can be bypassed. Things are going to get weird into the silver challenge though, don’t worry.

🧙‍♂️ Read your spells!
🧙‍♂️ Front gates are… Optional.

The silver challenge, aptly named “Malfunctionarium,” is a strange and difficult dungeon. Every enemy, and I mean EVERY enemy, will shuffle their positions on the map whenever ANY enemy takes damage. Not only this, but enemies with lifesteal will chunk your health when revealed. Luckily, there is a way to stop blinking enemies: slowing them. Use this to try to get monsters to stick around for 2 hits.

🧙‍♂️ Use Weytwut and Wonafyt to slow enemies and disable their blink
🧙‍♂️ Move towards the glyphs revealed by Magic Sense
🧙‍♂️ Wonafyt prioritises enemies in this order: Monsters that are not slowed, monsters that are the same level as the player, monsters that are a lower level then the player. There’s a trick you can do with this to slow the same monster multiple times. You’ll figure it out though, Harry.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/c99552abc89f606af3f23fe7d4699fa52ee8b282.gif[/img]

[h1]Basic tips for advancement[/h1]
Alright, this section should be short and sweet (don’t tell the Gnomes I said that.) Here are some hints on how to progress in the more “meta” sense.

[h3]Puzzles[/h3]
Puzzles are the tutorials of this game. Unlock a god? Play the puzzles to see how they work. No idea how attack priority works? Play the puzzles to get all the details. That Kin you unlocked seems bad? Play the puzzles to see how they can be useful. You’ll also get rewards to upgrade your kingdom!

[h3]Class Challenges[/h3]
As we’ve discussed, each class has challenges that teach you how to play them. Finishing the bronze challenge will give you gold, and finishing the silver challenge will give you an item that will start appearing in shops. Speaking of which…

[h3]Unlocking Shops[/h3]
While out and about, you might find a funny looking scroll. It summons a demon that serves an interdimensional being called Bezaar. Don’t, worry they have the best bargains in town! You’ll have to do a quest or two for them to get better items, so keep an eye out for those.

The Witch is another character you’ll come across. They’ll sell you potions and send you on weird quests for more potions. This will help you in dungeons.

[h3]Unlocking Gods[/h3]
Subdungeons are useful finds. They can contain gold, items, challenges, and snippets of lore. Sometimes, however, you’ll find one with an altar… Be wary of these rooms as they can be deadly, but overcoming the challenge or solving them will reward you with the presence of a God. These gods are fickle beings, and we’ll be writing a post on how to use them sometime soon!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/15af6723e0b61d7c703895b656254b339a1c93d8.gif[/img]

That's all for today! Release day is coming up fast, and we hope you're excited. Remember that if you own the original before 18th April, you'll get Rewind for free! 

If you want to check out the game before buying it, you can get small bites of it with our Demo... Daily!

notes.title: The Crusader - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #11
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/9b4a0adc8c99f28f5413f4c9633fe9dcf8d1ed6f.png[/img]

You wanna learn how to stack [i]momentum[/i]? How to stack those [i]profits[/i]? How to stack the heads of anyone that’s in your way? You’re in the right place. Crusaders are an unstoppable force, chain pulping losers that could never get where you are. Are you ready to learn the ways of the Crusader?

(if you somehow don't find this guide helpful, check out [url=https://www.qcfdesign.com/wiki/DesktopDungeons/index.php?title=Crusader]this link[/url] for better explanations)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/3b19a960587454d2941d8a614054163368a720ab.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Abilities[/b][/h2]
💯 [b]Scars [/b]- Poison Immune, Mana Burn Immune, Curse Immune

💯 [b]Momentum[/b]- Successive kills add 15% bonus damage. Levelling up or losing momentum halves bonus

💯 [b]Martyr[/b]- Extra altar spawn

[b]Momentum[/b]. Speed. Power. This is what the Crusader is all about. Stack 'em tall, knock' em down. When you land the killing blow on a monster, momentum will give you [b]15% bonus damage[/b]. Hitting a monster and not killing it, or levelling up, will [b]halve your momentum[/b]. It’s all about the momentum. Kill a couple of popcorn to get to bonus damage, and smash the boss’s face in. Level up, build more [i]momentum[/i], more [i]speed[/i], more [i]power[/i]. Smash the boss’s face again. Boss? More like, “hold that loss.” Because they’re a loser and you’re not.

We’re tough. Real tough. We’ve got [b]Scars[/b]. No more poison, no more mana burn, no more curse. Only [b]Momentum[/b]. These other classes need to get on our [i]level[/i]. We can fight Serpents, Wraiths, and Thralls without even caring, they’re so scared of us I’m surprised they even hit back. We can take out the toughest they have and not give a [i]damn[/i]. We’ve got [b]momentum[/b].

We’re gonna die for a cause. We’re [b]Martyrs[/b], and our cause is [b]momentum[/b]. You know we ride in the big leagues, with extra Deities around us. If they can’t give us anything, we disrespect them. Yeah, we’ll make our way through the punishment and take that Piety. Fast. We’ve got better options, bigger fish to catch. [b]Momentum[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/71f9ba9959f530e810e5b7f2d6b6f5391b6214e7.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Kin Choices[/b][/h2]
💯 [b]Orc [/b]- Momentum is a product of mass and velocity, and Orcs bring the [i]mass[/i]. Hit harder. Stack those gains and then stack those profits as you sell the head of that chump they call a “boss.” Loser. We’re using [b]mathematical formulas[/b] over here. Our base damage is [b]multiplied [/b]by our bonus damage. That means we get value from momentum with base damage. Yeah, we’re smart. We know how to grow conversion investments.

💯 [b]Halfling [/b]- Halflings have that grind-set investor lifestyle. Potions give us [i]mass[/i], our mindset gives us [i]speed[/i], and therefore we get that [b]momentum[/b]. Halflings are trading entrepreneurs. They’re artists at it, really. Invest your Health Potions in [b]Reflexes [/b]with Tikki T, or in [b]Piety [/b]with the [b]Glowing G[/b], or supplemental [b]Health Boosters[/b] with [b]big man JJ[/b]. They’re visionaries, really.

💯 [b]Goblin [/b]- If you’re not levelling up on the daily, you’re gonna lose at [i]life[/i]. Crusaders don’t lose. Goblins level up. Every. Single. [b]Day[/b]. Their conversion is supreme. You’ll lose your [b]momentum[/b], but pick yourself back up. Take that heal, rebuild your momentum, use that power.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/79ca2f013b0ea6380c84181e3dad4b669275f95e.png[/img]

[h2][b]Gods[/b][/h2]
💯 [b]Taurog [/b]- Our main man Taurog has [i]force[/i]. That’s why we like him. We stack the bodies of losers and Taurog gives us the drip we need to do our job. We’re out here doing damage to these dungeons while looking good in [b]Gloat [/b]and [b]Will[/b]. Smashing people with [b]Skullpicker [/b]and the [b]Wereward[/b]. [i]Momentum[/i]. With Taurog, we’re an [b]Unstoppable Fury[/b]. Literally.

💯 [b]Dracul [/b]- Drac knows everyone is below us. Drac also knows that there’s no point feeling bad for them. This is [i]our world[/i], they're just living in it. Levelling up makes us lose our momentum, but gives us health. Drac cuts out the middleman and [b]heals us straight up[/b] with [b]Blood Swell[/b] so we can keep our streak. You know we’re hungry for success, and [b]Blood Hunger[/b] keeps us full. It’s called “life steal,” but we think of it more as “life repurposing” because they weren’t doing much with it.

💯 [b]Tikki Tooki[/b] - Power is work divided by time. Tikki makes work happen in no time. That’s right, the amount of power is [i]undefinable[/i]. He likes it when we take out the little guys. He knows that’s what they weren’t going anywhere, just wasting space on your dungeon floor. In return, we get the speed to dodge attacks, the Reflexes to hit harder, and Tikki’s Edge to learn how to level up faster. That’s momentum. Never forget it.

And for those Gods that have nothing to offer us… Disrespect them. [b]Desecrate [/b]their altars. [b]Earthmother[/b]? Yeah we’ll take that 30 piety and chug a Burn Salve to get rid of the corrosion. [b]Binlor[/b]? Yeah take my resists, I didn’t have them anyways. Just make sure you don’t mess with the [b]Glowing G [/b]- actually, nevermind. [i]Try it and let us know how it goes lil' bro[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/d5e97b2d3642a68ff11e02aa28b107d54ffba05d.png[/img]

[h2][b]Glyphs[/b][/h2]
💯 [b]Pisorf [/b]- You know what doesn’t kill momentum? Getting people out of our way. [b]Pisorf[/b]! We’ve got things to do, and your face needs to meet that [i]wall[/i]. Damage? Check. Momentum? Also check.

💯 [b]Bysseps [/b]- It’s all about the [i]numbers[/i]. The numbers don’t lie, and they spell disaster for your enemies. Bysseps gives us more numbers, 30 of them to be exact, which are all added to our bonus damage. If they’re trying to resist you, you’ll slowly take that away from them as well. We got a 144 2⁄3% chance of winnin'.

Most Glyphs are useful to us, but be careful with [b]Burndayraz [/b]as it’ll break your momentum. Now that’s not fire. Make sure to use Glyphs to hustle some [b]Piety [/b]for your main G(od).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43475627/b76e2d84c769c0452b9617972029f3f929915ca1.png[/img]

And that's all there is to it. Remember to subscribe to the Crusader newsletter and buy our online course to get more in depth advice for only [strike]999[/strike] 499 gold! This is a limited time offer. Use your momentum to get it.

notes.title: The Gorgon - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #10
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/b4bd64b1006a7773702b57cf51cf78b3be5851c0.png[/img]

We’ve done it! We’ve reached [b]10 class posts[/b]! Thanks for reading them and we hope they’ve helped you get your Dailies done. Speaking of Dailies, we’ve just pushed a patch that fixes a lot of issues and buffs up the functionality of the leaderboard, so make sure to check it out.

To celebrate, we’re looking at a monster class voted on by Twitter. This week, slithering into the mix, is the Gorgon! They're simple to explain but hard to play, with an irresistible gaze and an amazing hairstyle. Let’sss get into it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/6e0b6a7921860c094c9a74dbb184c3f395d3221b.gif[/img]

[h1][b]Abilitiesss[/b][/h1]
🐍 [b]Azure Body[/b] - Starts with 25% Physical resist, Death Gaze Immune, -50% bonus damage

🐍 [b]Sapphire Locks[/b] - Natural Poisonous strike, petrifies enemies, starts with ENDISWAL glyph

🐍 [b]Amethyst Stare[/b] - Starts with Death-gaze 10%. Death-gaze effect deals unresistable damage upon attacking enemies with low health.

Much like we sssaid with the Monk and Paladin, the physical resistances from [b]Azure Body[/b] make you better at [b]regen fighting[/b]! This combined with your naturally [b]poisonousss strikes[/b] from [b]Sapphire Locks[/b] means you can often take down high level physical damage enemies. 

As a Gorgon, you are immune to Death Gaze and have your own Snake Stare (thanks Serafs!) [b]Amethyst Stare[/b] gives you [b]Death Gaze[/b], and your conversions increase the % at which you’ll execute. When enemies are below your threshold your next attack deals [b]unresistable damage[/b]. If this kills them they'll be petrified, leaving their remains behind. You’ll need to get rid of their remains with [b]Endiswal[/b].

[b]-50% bonus damage[/b] from Azure Body is a hefty penalty, but can be overcome with some items (or a very fun Binlor strategy!) You can also bypass this by holding onto [b]Burndayraz[/b], which will switch up your damage profile, slow regen enemy with Burning to make poison last longer, and deal damage that increases with your level.

Before we continue, here are some notes on [b]Poisonous Strike[/b]: [list]
[*] For each stack of Poisoned, enemies will not regenerate [b]one health[/b].
[*] [b]Exploring [/b]to heal will [b]remove [/b]Poisoned stacks from enemies.
[*] [b]Undead [/b]enemies cannot be poisoned.
[*] Poisonous Strike inflicts Poison stacks equal to [b]five times your level[/b].
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/33e56cfcdff4654c5eb3e0cd7b164f508d8047f9.gif[/img]

[h1][b]Godsss[/b][/h1]
🐍 [b]Binlor Ironshield[/b] - Starting with the [b]Endiswal [/b]Glyph, we can easily build up some Piety for Binlor. What are we going to do with this piety? We’re going to buy [b]Stone Form[/b]! (This irony is not lost on us.) Stone Form will give us [b]Might [/b]whenever we [b]destroy a wall,[/b] counteracting the -50% bonus damage penalty. [b]Stone Fist[/b] can also be bought to [b]knockback[/b] enemies into walls, and with Poisonous Strike you don’t need to worry about them regenerating while you chase them down. Your petrified enemies near Binlor’s altar will be destroyed when you buy Boons.

🐍 [b]The Earthmother[/b] - Most regen fighters enjoy Earthmother because of the [b]damage reduction[/b] from [b]Vine Form[/b], and the Gorgon is no different. [b]Greenblood [/b]is also useful, as corroding enemies will significantly boost your damage throughout a fight. There is some slight anti-sssynergy as your petrified enemies block Blood Pools for [b]Plantation[/b].

🐍 [b]Mystera Annur[/b] - Mystera will reward you with piety for casting glyphs, and you’ll be using [b]Endiswal [/b]plenty! [b]Mystic Balance[/b] will reduce the cost of Endiswal and Burndayraz, and [b]Magic [/b]is always useful. However, [b]Weakening [/b]will take away your physical resistance and [b]Flames [/b]will render your attacks almost uselesss.

Two other Deitiesss to keep in mind are [b]Taurog [/b](for more resistances and damage) and [b]Dracul [/b](for the usual Dracul late game spike.) Whatever you do, don’t worship[b] Glowing Guar[/b]-... actually nevermind. Just try it and see how it goes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/3bb55fde6f8554d1dab23f2b9040448d7ef83a8a.png[/img]

[h1][b]Glyphsss[/b][/h1]
🐍 [b]Imawal [/b]- Because you know what we need? That, right, [b]more petrification[/b]! Because your main strategy is hunting down high level enemies that deal physical damage, using Imawal on a low level enemy will give you a pretty big [b]experience boost[/b]. Fully worth the 5 mana, and you already have Endiswal to clear the remains.

🐍 [b]Burndayraz [/b]- Fireballs mix up your damage type, bypass the penalty from [b]Azure Body[/b], and apply Burning. Burning makes enemies [b]heal [/b]as if they were [b]one level lower[/b]. Less regen means that your stacks of [b]poison last longer[/b]!

🐍 [b]Halpmeh [/b]- Healing up in the middle of a fight can help you to build up more poison on higher level enemies, which in turn lets you explore for more health and mana. Keep that train going and they’re going to be the ones needing halp!

Obviously you’ll be using [b]Endiswal [/b]all the time when cleaning up leftoversss and making your way around the dungeon, while using the Stone Skin it gives you to tank big hits. [b]Getindare [/b]and [b]Weytwut [/b]lose a bit of value because of your Death Gaze pseudo-execute. They're still useful in some situations, and Weytwut can be used to line up the Binlor combo.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/c372b587ffc593dab4c3c28bce1ae02d7ff5f08f.png[/img]

[h1][b]Strategiesss[/b][/h1]
So which prey are you going to be looking for as a Gorgon? Here are the best snacks around that you’ll be able to munch on:

🐍 You win the mirror match with [b]Gorgons[/b]. (This irony is not lost on us.) Your immunity to their Death Gaze combined with their physical damage and relatively low health makes them easy pickings. 

🐍 [b]Meat Men[/b] are defined by their large health bars and low damage. This is great for building up your poison and outhealing them with exploring.

🐍 Lessser snakes, called [b]Serpents[/b], can be handled with ease so long as you have a level up or [b]Halpmeh [/b]ready to clear their poison.

You’ll struggle more with [b]undead [/b]enemies who can’t be poisoned and enemies that deal magic damage. [b]Zombies [/b]hit hard, but at least they deal physical damage which you can resist. [b]Wraiths [/b]on the other hand will deal magic damage, can’t be poisoned, resist physical attacks, AND will mana burn you. Do not engage unless you have [b]Burndayraz[/b]. [b]Bandits [/b]are manageable, but will [b]Curse [/b]away your physical resistances for a while. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/3b000631865ab7a8b96b733ed11a168576da0f10.png[/img]

That'sss all for today! My "S" key on my keyboard has been acting up, sorry about that.

notes.title: The Paladin - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #9
notes.content:
[i]“Paladins are state-sanctioned spiritual warriors who can smack foes across the head with either sword or scripture depending on what the situation demands. They tend to be unbearably smug about it.”[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/77b4da5e51ea57c06cf0f715baaf5e4aea55aa74.png[/img]

Returning for another class post, lead by a higher power, we're talking about the Paladin! Are you a fan of commitment? Do you like carrying out the will of divine beings? Well this week’s class is for you! Play the Paladin, pledge your allegiance to your one true Deity, and do their bidding to win your run.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/fe61a8731111086a9fb20aa914b9f74fd67a6b57.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Abilities[/b][/h2]
📜 [b]Holy Work[/b] - Cannot switch religions. God boons are 20% cheaper. Gods do not punish.

📜 [b]Holy Hands[/b] - Starts with the Halpmeh glyph, regains +1 HP/level with it.

📜 [b]Holy Shield[/b] - Starts with 25% Physical resistance.

Let's start with a short writ about [b]Gods [/b]in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind. When you [b]worship [/b]a God you have access to their [b]boons[/b], which cost piety. You can gain piety by taking actions your God likes and lose piety by blaspheming. If you go below 0 piety, you will be heavily [b]punished [/b]by your God. You can also [b]desecrate [/b]the altars of other Gods to appease your own, or [b]convert [/b]to worship them instead. Converting costs half of your piety and you must have at least 50 piety. 

[b]Holy Work[/b] is the defining feature of the Paladin class. While most other classes waltz around the pantheon and make Gods work for them, Paladins know what’s right: [b]monotheism[/b]. They’re rewarded with [b]cheaper boons[/b] and [b]forgiven for their sins[/b] when at 0 piety. Playing around not being punished is essential and makes the Paladin very flexible.

[b]Holy Hands[/b] and [b]Holy Shield[/b] work together to make the paladin a formidable force for delivering divine retribution. Healing with [b]resistances [/b]gives more effective health, and [b]regen fighting[/b] is a strong option as you can convert the mana you gain into health with [b]Halpmeh[/b]. Pick off higher level enemies that deal physical damage with ease!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/ad69d94f3b81f89669dd5821358cf2dd7f320445.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Kin Choices[/b][/h2]
📜 [b]Elves [/b]- Elves make for amazing vassals due to their [b]conversions giving them mana[/b]. Being able to cast [b]Halpmeh [/b]three to four times in a fight will give you two health bars to play with, taking down the fiercest of foes. Does an enemy have physical resistance? No problem! Use your bonus mana to burn them with holy [b]fireballs[/b]. Just make sure your Deity appreciates your Glyph casting habits and you’ll be set. 

📜 [b]Orcs [/b]- Orcs bring a little muscle to the Paladin’s holy house. With [b]bonus base damage from conversion[/b], [b]regen fighting[/b] can make them a menace at all points in a Dungeon. As strikers, they excel at worshipping Gods like [b]Taurog [/b]or [b]Binlor [/b]that help you hit things. [b]Glowing Guardian[/b] can also help you break through  high physical resistances with [b]Cleansing[/b].

📜 [b]Halfling [/b]- Bringing their own potions to their dungeon pilgrimage, Halflings can play in creative ways while worshipping. [b]Glowing Guardian[/b] and [b]Dracul [/b]will usually punish you for drinking potions, but Paladins can ignore this downside if they have no piety to lose. These extra health potions can also be given to [b]Tikki Tooki [/b]for [b]Reflexes [/b]or to [b]Jehora Jeheyu [/b]for [b]Boost Health[/b]. Having more health from worshipping [b]Earthmother [/b]will make health potions more effective, and having them available after [b]Taurog [/b]reduces your mana makes both great Deities a great option.

As per usual, [b]Humans [/b]can be played much the same way as Orcs. [b]Gnomes [/b]create mana potions, and can be played similarly to Elves or Halflings. [b]Dwarves [/b]are alright, but Halpmeh’s heal does not scale with maximum health so there isn’t much synergy outside of having more health for resistances.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/635ed73eb69b9de4356297d570505d6ed0780356.png[/img]

[h2][b]Gods[/b][/h2]
📜 [b]Glowing Guardian[/b] - Being punished by GG will remove everything in your inventory and often end your run… But [b]no longer[/b]! As a Paladin, you can [b]farm piety[/b] by healing poison with [b]Halpmeh[/b] to grow your collection of [b]prayer beads[/b] and reach [b]Enlightenment [/b]for a massive late game spike. [b]Cleansing[/b], [b]Protection[/b], and [b]Absolution [/b]will keep you healthy. All at 20% off! 

📜 [b]Taurog [/b]- Wrath is your path, trodden by many and survived by few. But with Taurog at your side, you’ll be [b]armed to the teeth[/b] with weapons of war and given the gift of becoming an [b]Unstoppable Fury[/b]! With the reduced cost of boons, picking up [b]Taurog’s gear[/b] is fast and simple, turning you into a powerhouse of violence. Be careful, your fire is fierce but can often be short lived, and you might struggle with [b]less mana[/b] later into the run.

📜 [b]Pactmaker [/b]- This is a new face to the pantheon! Pactmaker isn’t “someone” you “worship,” they are simply a force to be [b]bargained with[/b]. When certain conditions are met, they will [b]take your piety[/b] and [b]provide you with a bonus[/b]. For example, [b]Body Pact[/b] will give you [b]resistances [/b]whenever you are [b]damaged[/b], and will cost you 4 piety. No piety, no bonus. As Paladins have more piety than other classes, Pactmaker can passively ramp up their strength through a run. Drinking potions? [b]Alchemists Pact[/b]. Converting Items?[b] Spirit Pact[/b]. This is for your own strength… Right?

While we’ve highlighted these three Gods, there are many ways to worship each Deity, and each will come with a different way to play. Some deity choices are better suited to [b]different Kin[/b], so if you aren’t preparing an altar, keep your mind open to the possibilities!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/a256604203910b5f222360689f9352d47bc8fe7a.png[/img]

[h2][b]Glyphs[/b][/h2]
📜 [b]Halpmeh [/b]- The butter to your holy bread, Halpmeh is your defining glyph. When cast it heals you for [b]5 health per level[/b], letting you fight longer and take down higher level monsters. That’s really all there is to it! Remember that each mana you gain effectively heals your level in health, so you’re regening as if you were [b]one level higher[/b]. 

📜 [b]Bysseps [/b]- If your strategy is hitting things over and over again, [b]bigger arms always help[/b]. Bysseps can be cast in between each hit for a 30% damage boost, and will also [b]shred [/b]through enemy [b]resistances [/b]by [b]3%[/b] with each hit. This will help whittle down enemies with high physical resistances.

These two Glyphs are useful for most gods, and after that you’ll see your Glyphs change based on [b]Deity[/b]. For example, you’ll use [b]Pisorf [/b]while worshipping [b]Binlor[/b], some [b]Burndayraz [/b]casts to give [b]Glowing Guardian[/b] a burnt offering, or [b]Imawal [/b]to make the [b]Earthmother’s [/b]forest permanent.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/15fb33c026e096c2c7cca0280d494119766c673c.png[/img]

That's all for today! While all Paladins worship their own Deity, they realise that each faith is valid and respect each other for their choices. 💕

notes.title: The Bloodmage - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #8
notes.content:
[i]“Bloodmages are the mad scientists of the magic-using world: essentially the Sorcerer gone a little bit rotten. Not rotten enough to be considered un-heroic, but still not the sort of person you'd want to meet in a shadowy alchemy lab.”[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/3b4ee85f537338b13b5685de63d5064043c98532.png[/img]

Welcome to the 8th Desktop Dungeons: Rewind class post! Let’s dive into the class with the fastest way to your heart… The Bloodmage! Corrupted by magic and driven insane by a thirst for power, they’re guaranteed to find a way under any enemy’s skin.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/fff7c125a4f4839f97eeb6c4f8ffd365c9687064.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Abilities[/b][/h2]
🩸 [b]Power Hungry[/b] -  Mana Potions are 60% effective and boost Sanguine

🩸 [b]Sanguine [/b]- Starts with Sanguine 20% buff, drinking blood restores 1 mana

🩸 [b]Insane[/b] - Starts with the Bludtupowa glyph, -3 max mana

Bloodmages unlock a new resource to play with: [b]blood pools[/b]. Killing an enemy that is not bloodless will leave a blood pool on the dungeon floor. With the [b]Sanguine [/b]trait, Bloodmages can consume them to [b]regain [/b]20% of their [b]health [/b]and one [b]mana[/b]! This can be used mid-fight to heal up for another hit or get enough mana for a Glyph cast. Either way, the rivers will run red.

[b]Power Hungry[/b] makes [b]Mana Potions[/b] the Bloodmage’s second favourite drink (after a home-made Bloody Mary.) Instead of restoring 40% of your mana they will restore 60% to balance out the penalty from [b]Insane[/b]. More importantly, they increase the amount of health restored by [b]Sanguine [/b]by two percent! This can make saving your blood pools until after drinking Mana potions an efficient choice if you don’t want to clot your run.

[b]Insane [/b]gives the Bloodmage a free [b]Bludtupowa [/b]Glyph at the start of each run. Bludtupowa is a unique Glyph: it reveals tiles without healing monsters, deals damage to your character, and restores mana. Trading your [b]health for mana[/b] and making use of [b]Sanguine [/b]can allow a Bloodmage to unleash a string of fireballs like no other class. This comes at the cost of having -3 maximum mana, but this can be played around.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/97b4b402ef83f0f6a243589d058f1ecc7f3c7c9d.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Kin Choices[/b][/h2]
🩸 [b]Human [/b]- Ah, humans. Always the versatile option! Humans are good at playing with what they get, they really are universal receivers. They can spike well in the late game with their [b]conversion bonus[/b] and damage items, while letting [b]Burndayraz [/b]and [b]Pisorf [/b]help them through the early game. Once you’ve run out of tiles to explore, you’ll often be able to convert your Glyphs and pummel bosses in between blood sippin’ sessions.

🩸 [b]Dwarf [/b]- Bigger bodies means more blood. Pretty simple! When Dwarves convert items they [b]gain health[/b], which works fantastically with [b]Sanguine[/b]. With more efficient blood pools, you can repeatedly throw yourself at anything in your way and probably win. Dwarf Bloodmages can get so tanky that the only blood monsters will draw is with a red crayon!

🩸 [b]Gnome [/b]- I guess they are called Blood[i]mages[/i], so let’s talk about a Kin that plays around Glyphs. Gnomes can create their own [b]Mana Potions[/b] when converting items, which doubles down on synergy: you have [b]more mana[/b] to cast spells because of [b]Power Hungry[/b], and you regain [b]more health[/b] from the improvements to [b]Sanguine[/b]. Anything that stands in your way is going to bleed and burn as you switch between fireballs and fists, all while restoring large chunks of mana and health. 

In general, Bloodmages are a very versatile class and can be played however you want. In the same vein as the Human, [b]Orcs [/b]can make a good choice of Striker with a better early game but more of a reliance on [b]Pisorf[/b]. [b]Halflings [/b]are a similar type to Dwarves, making HP out of nowhere with [b]Health Potions[/b]. Finally, [b]Elves [/b]can make great casters in place of Gnomes as their [b]bonus mana[/b] can clot the penalty of Insane.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/f0cd012ba59b35aa344f8ffe42bd7b0a91520a2c.png[/img]

[h2][b]Gods[/b][/h2]
🩸 [b]Jehora Jeheyu[/b] - Unsurprisingly, the God of Madness is a good fit for the Mad Mages. [b]Boost Health[/b] lets you trade a Health Potion for more maximum health which makes [b]Sanguine [/b]more effective, and [b]Boost Mana[/b] can help balance out the penalty from [b]Insane[/b]. Losing a Mana Potion from Boost Mana can feel bad unless you’re playing a [b]Gnome[/b], but it’s usually worthwhile. 

🩸 [b]Dracul [/b]- The God of Undeath himself, and the only way other classes can gain access to Sanguine. Late game, you’ll be playing around your [b]blood pools[/b] anyways, so a Dracul conversion can be a good choice for [b]Strikers [/b]to access Life Steal and buffed Sanguine. Blood on blood, baby!

🩸 [b]Binlor Ironshield[/b] - As per usual, [b]resistances [/b]are great for adventurers that restore health. [b]Pisorf [/b]is also a good damage spell, and its lower cost fits well with the Bloodmages reduced mana pool. However, winning with Binlor late game is like drawing blood from a stone, so it’s usually wise to build up Piety and resistances before [b]converting [/b]to another deity like Mystera or Dracul. 

Whatever you do… [b]Do not worship Glowing Guardian[/b]! He’ll punish you heavily for using Bludtupowa and slurping on your favourite forbidden sauce, which means you’ll likely end up losing all of your items. Just don’t do it. [b]Mystera [/b]can be a good choice for Elves and Gnomes who can spam fireballs, and [b]Earthmother [/b]is a useful god as Vine Form and Entanglement can make your run a lot smoother.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/e78a80dfa3a9fd93b41f1217ef4276c22e19a89d.png[/img]

[h2][b]Glyphs[/b][/h2]
🩸 [b]Bludtupowa [/b]- It’s time to talk about Bludtupowa. Let’s talk about exactly how it works: on activation it deals [b]damage to the player[/b] equal to three times their level. It also [b]reveals the three nearest unrevealed tiles[/b] and [b]restores three mana[/b]. Monsters and the player do not regenerate from the tiles being revealed by this Glyph. Trading health for mana is useful when your health doesn’t matter. For example, if you’d die on a monster’s next hit, you can cast Bludtupowa to land the final blow with a [b]Burdayraz [/b]or cast [b]Getindare[/b]. This trade is also worthwhile if your main strategy is casting [b]Glyphs for damage[/b], and allows you to use Bludtupowa and [b]Sanguine [/b]as an engine to [b]pump [/b]out damage.

🩸 [b]Getindare [/b]- Both Bloodmage Casters and Strikers can benefit from Getindare. As a Caster, cast Getindare [b]before combat[/b] and explore to restore mana before beginning. Start the fireball fiesta and use the saved Getindare to make the last attack from safety. Getindare is the perfect mana cost for the amount restored by Bludtupowa, and so it can be used for important final hits when playing in a Striker style.

🩸 [b]Weytwut [/b]- Making the Glyph list for its synergy with [b]Pisorf[/b], Weytwut can be used to [b]set-up[/b] an enemy next to a wall or another enemy before sending them into the grinder. Orcs work best with this strategy as their base damage from conversions powers up Pisorf. Against two bosses this combo can win a dungeon, so hold on to Weytwut if you find it!

As usual, [b]Burndayraz [/b]and [b]Pisorf [/b]are the Glyphs at the heart of your attack strategy. [b]Wonafyt [/b]can function similarly to Weytwut in a pinch, and [b]Endiswal [/b]can help with set-up. [b]Bysseps [/b]can be used effectively on Strikers, but casters will find little use for it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/034f33808b5fd50f343aa8ba8493895103084f5e.png[/img]

That’s it for today! If you're healthy, remember that donating blood saves lives. World Blood Donor day is in June, so get started early 💓
