notes.title: The Assassin - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #7
notes.content:
[h3]Wait… Did you hear that? [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/0e511c7299d5d3d727103d294358405bc8cf1ebc.png[/img]

Of course you didn’t! Welcome back to another Desktop Dungeons: Rewind class post! This week we’ll be looking at the Assassin: a poisonous professional with a propensity for dispatching plebs. Sneak your way around enemies and slice 'em to pieces!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/9a3f185aae1fe74983f6f8077ff982da437a2057.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Abilities[/b][/h2]
🐱‍👤 [b]Poisoned Blade[/b] - Free Glyph: APHEELSIK, 40% bonus damage vs poisoned monsters

🐱‍👤 [b]Light Foot[/b] - Exploring the area around a monster grants First Strike

🐱‍👤 [b]Swift Hand[/b] - Starting attack penalty, attacking lower level monster is instant kill

Assassins are a hit squad all on their own that can be played in a variety of ways. They can be played as [b]Strikers[/b], relying on their regen fighting prowess, or [b]Casters[/b], making the best of their ability to oneshot lower level enemies. Being flexible and going for a [b]Hybrid [/b]of these two is also viable.

[b]Poisoned Blade[/b] gives the Assassin a free [b]Apheelsik [/b]glyph at the start of each run. Apheelsik [b]poisons [/b]enemies, which [b]stops their regeneration[/b] for an amount of health based on your level. This helps the Assassin to attack enemies and explore without enemies regenerating health! Apheelsik synergises well with [b]Light Foot[/b], as you’ll want to reveal the area around an enemy to have access to [b]First Strike[/b]. As a final nail in their coffin, you’ll deal bonus damage to poisoned enemies.

[b]Swift Hand[/b] is the Assassin class's defining feature: attacking any enemy that is a lower level than you will [b]instantly kill[/b] them, regardless of how much damage you have. Interestingly, this ability is what makes a [b]Caster [/b]build viable! Most Casters will neglect their attacks in favour of spell damage, which can make killing lower level enemies (nicknamed “[b]popcorn[/b]”) cost health for attacks or mana for Glyphs, and therefore cost black space. Swift Hand can also make [b]levelling [/b]during a fight for the healing very easy, as killing popcorn is automatic.

On the flip side, Swift Hand also gives a [b]penalty [/b]to your starting attack bonus. This means that you rely on poisoning an enemy to deal more [b]damage [/b]with attacks. Playing around this usually involves your [b]kin [/b]choice, which we’ll get into now!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/5475596c9d718a7683ba14aeea0b5fdd86139b48.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Kin Choices[/b][/h2]
🐱‍👤 [b]Human[/b] - Make for a great choice when planning to play a [b]Striker [/b]build, as their conversion bonus of 10% damage can offset the attack penalty from Swift Hand. You’ll still need [b]Glyphs [/b]like Apheelsik, Bysseps, and Burndayraz to take down tough foes, so stay flexible throughout your run and be willing to play a [b]Hybrid [/b]depending on what you find!

🐱‍👤 [b]Elf [/b]- Elves favour a [b]Caster [/b]build with their conversion bonus providing a boost to your maximum mana. Finding a [b]Burndayraz [/b]during the mid levels of your run is important, so you might consider preparing [b]Flame Magnet[/b]. Instead of poisoning enemies to regain your health, you’ll be doing it for mana to fling fireballs. Instantly killing lower level monsters means you don’t need to worry about [b]wasting space[/b] to heal or restore mana!

🐱‍👤 [b]Goblin [/b]- Welcoming a new Kin to the Class Posts, we have the Goblin! Goblins are a very unique Kin, as they gain [b]experience[/b] from converting items. This sneaky boost to your levels makes [b]Swift Hand[/b] incredibly strong. Goblin Assassins can set themselves up to level up [b]many times[/b] in a single fight, giving them refreshers on their health. Watch a boss deal with [i]that[/i]!

As an alternative to Humans, [b]Orcs [/b]can make for great Strikers at the cost of versatility. Orcs don’t do very well with Hybrid Assassin builds. If you don’t feel like playing an Elf, [b]Gnomes [/b]make for a decent substitute. It’s a bit of a downgrade, but if you can prepare items that synergise well with potions like [b]Trisword [/b]it can be a slight upgrade.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/03c7931365cbe16581c1b3133d8046eff12c0905.png[/img]

[h2][b]Gods[/b][/h2]
🐱‍👤 [b]Tikki Tooki[/b] - Well if we’re killing for something, it’s probably money (or [b]experience[/b], in the case of interning Assassins.) Tikki is a difficult god to manage early into a run because he’ll [b]punish [/b]you for being hit multiple times by the same enemy. No regen fighting for you… What makes him good to worship is [b]Tikki’s Edge[/b], which gives you [b]bonus experience[/b] on kill. When you’re snacking on your [b]popcorn [/b]with your [b]Swift Hands[/b], this stacks up fast. Any piety you have left over can be spent on [b]potions [/b]to spike for a boss fight.

🐱‍👤 [b]Mystera Annur[/b] - Assassins can make great casters because of their ability to kill lower level enemies with a snap of their fingers. Getting mana from Mystera through [b]Magic [/b]can make for a couple more spell casts, and using [b]Weakening [/b]to crack through resistances is amazing! And just like that, they disappear… Magic!

🐱‍👤 [b]Dracul[/b] - We haven’t talked about Dracul in a class post yet. This is mostly because he’s a [b]big scary vampire man[/b], but it’s also because he’s used as a [b]late-game transition[/b] to kill a boss. [b]Blood Tithe[/b] allows you to drink blood pools for health, and [b]Blood Swell[/b] can provide you with a full health refresh if you don’t care about being cursed. Having access to blood pools is guaranteed as the Assassin because of [b]Swift Hand[/b], and refilling with health during a boss fight is very valuable. However, assassins are terrible at using [b]Life Steal[/b] (insta-killing things has a downside, who would have thought!) and so [b]Blood Hunger[/b] isn’t useful. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/906f4fcd31c9a0bf68993f88760183992bc0f75b.png[/img]

[h2][b]Glyphs[/b][/h2]
🐱‍👤 [b]Apheelsik [/b]- This Glyph is so important for the class that you start with one [b]for free[/b]! Use it frequently to unlock your full potential. Poison, attack, regenerate, attack. [b]Rinse and repeat[/b] until your target is nothing but a pile of poisonous chunks! [i]They’ll never see it coming...[/i]
🐱‍👤 [b]Burndayraz [/b]- Ah, good old Fireballs. Assassins are the sneakiest demolition experts, and can use fireballs as [b]finishers [/b]or [b]consistent damage[/b] depending on their [b]build[/b]. Undead enemies can’t be [b]poisoned[/b], and so using Burndayraz as your [b]heal negation[/b] for these enemies will help regen fighting and damage.
🐱‍👤 [b]Wonafyt [/b]- Wonafyt summons a monster from the dungeon that is the same level as you and [b]slows [/b]them. If there are no monsters the same level as you, it will teleport[b] lower level[/b] monsters… And we know how fights go for lower level monsters! This Glyph has amazing synergy with [b]Tikki Tooki[/b]: he rewards you for [b]casting [/b]it, and further rewards you for [b]killing [/b]experience valuable low level enemies. Slowed enemies are considered to be [b]experience valuable[/b]… So get to summonin' and slicin’!

Having innate first strike from [b]Light Foot[/b] devalues Glyphs like [b]Getindare[/b] and [b]Weytwut[/b], so don't be afraid to convert them early (although Weytwut can get rid of an enemy's [b]First Strike[/b]!) [b]Imawal [/b]is always useful when trying to level up, especially if you're taking down higher level enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/4fac0be2e20a29154b0f16c14a501e083a55e85b.png[/img]

And that's it for this week. To play the Assassin ASAP, [b]wishlist Desktop Dungeons: Rewind![/b] Also make sure to follow our [url=https://twitter.com/QCFdesign]Twitter[/url], join our [url=https://discord.gg/KU2fHZX]Discord[/url], and play the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2232060/Desktop_Dungeons_Rewind__Daily_Demo/]Daily Demo[/url].

notes.title: The Rat Monarch - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #6
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/b477f78079cf53e366d578ae487ce6364634dbb8.png[/img]

[h3]Welcome back to the first Class Post of 2023! 
[/h3]
This week we’ll be looking at the most royal class in all of Desktop Dungeons: Rewind, the Rat Monarch. Are you ready to nibble your opponents to death with the power of supreme dental hygiene?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/ced39348cf35f694110162e5b6d749e70f54dd11.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Abilities[/b][/h2]
🧀 [b]Regal Hygiene[/b] - Rat bites corrode enemies. Gains one stack of Corrosive Strike per level.

🧀 [b]Regal Perks[/b] - Sensitive whiskers detect deals. All shops are scouted. Buying an item regenerates 50% health and mana (may overheal)

🧀 [b]Regal Size[/b] - Rats are the CORRECT size: Small. Lower maximum health and mana, all items are large.

Before we venture deeper into the Rat Monarch, we need to know what the [b]Corrosion [/b]status is and how it works. When a monster is corroded, it takes [b]extra damage equal to its corrosion on hit[/b]. This extra damage is also applied on spells, and can ramp up very high at later levels! 

[b]Regal Hygiene[/b] allows Rat Monarchs to give corrosion to an enemy [b]on attack[/b]. The amount of corrosion applied increases by 1 per level (and 1 per 80 Conversion Points!) For example, if a [b]level two[/b] Rat Monarch attacks a monster, that monster will now have [b]two corrosion[/b]. The second attack will deal two extra damage from corrosion and apply two more stacks of corrosion, which means a third attack will deal [b]four extra damage[/b]. Stacking corrosion is the main way that the Rat Monarch kills things!

[b]Regal Size[/b] reduces Rat Monarch’s base damage, mana, and health. The reduction of base damage means that building up corrosion on enemies is your main way of killing them. Corrosion does not go away, meaning you can build corrosion by fighting, exploring to heal up, rinse, and repeat, until you’re able to kill the monster.

The second element of Regal Size is that all items are [b]large items[/b], so let's talk about inventory size in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind. Your inventory is made up of [b]30 slots[/b], and each large item you are carrying fills [b]five slots[/b] while small items only fill [b]one[/b]. Potions are usually small items, but not to the Rat. This means that inventory management can become tricky, especially when wanting to make use of [b]Regal Perks[/b].

[b]Regal Perks[/b] is here to help the Rat Monarch heal up while fighting enemies. One issue being that... You need inventory space to buy an item, and we’re already a little short on that. You’ll be making decisions about which items you’ll be holding onto throughout each run, and timing your spending to get value out of the healing. You’ll be [b]converting [/b]the items you don’t need, making your [b]corrosive nibbles stronge[/b]r!

[b]Regal Perks[/b] also shows the locations of shops on the map. This is very useful for conserving tiles for regen fighting (check out our Monk post to learn about that!) 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/53d8c9ba41169a454b97de0a60bef92728db493f.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Gods[/b][/h2]
🧀 [b]Binlor Ironshield[/b] - Binlor is one of the best Gods to worship as the Rat Monarch. Binlor gives damage resistance through [b]Stone Skin[/b] and [b]Stone Form[/b], which lets the rat build up corrosion while saving tiles to regen on later. The second reason is that the Rat has incredible synergy with [b]Pisorf[/b] and [b]Stone Fist[/b], but we’ll get to that later… All in all, the God of Mining is here to help!

🧀 [b]Mystera Annur[/b] - Rats like to attack things. Not for damage, but to build corrosion! Damage from spells benefits from corrosion, and so Mystera becomes a great choice to worship. [b]Flames [/b]reduces your base damage and increases the damage of [b]Burndayraz[/b], making it great for the rat who doesn’t care about base damage. Magic can also help you to cast [b]Pisorf [/b]and [b]Burndayraz [/b]more often.

🧀 [b]Jehora Jeheyu[/b] - Jehora lets you exchange your Health and Mana Potions for [b]permanent boosts to health and mana[/b]. This covers up the weaknesses from [b]Regal Size[/b] through increasing your stats and freeing up your inventory slots.

[b]The Earthmother[/b] is another reasonable God because [b]Vine Form[/b] boosts health and gives damage reduction, but Rats have issues with getting value out of [b]Plantation [/b]because they struggle to kill weaker enemies quickly. [b]Entanglement [/b]is also average because slowing enemies isn’t very beneficial.

Make sure to avoid worshipping [b]Tikki Tooki[/b] and [b]Taurog[/b]! Tikki punishes the player when they are hit multiple[b] times by the same enemy[/b], which rats love to do, and Taurog fills your inventory with sub-par items while punishing you for using [b]glyphs[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/18f012d9dd4586f364937cf46cb43ac080d74d2f.png[/img]

[h2][b]Glyphs[/b][/h2]
🧀 [b]Pisorf [/b]- [b]Knockback [/b]is one of the most important things for Rats to have, and Pisorf is a great way to get it. Are you really a monarch if you aren’t pushing your subjects around? Pisorf is important because of how it [b]interacts with corrosion[/b]. If you apply lots of corrosion to a monster and push it into another monster, you’ll deal the [b]corrosion [/b]damage to [u]both of them[/u]! 

🧀 [b]Burndayraz [/b]- No matter what build you’re cooking up, you’ll need fire. Burndayraz is great for the Rat as it allows you to trigger your corrosion damage without getting attacked, making it a great finisher for your combos! The Burning debuff can also be useful for regen fighting.

These are the main glyphs you’ll be holding onto, especially with your limited inventory space from [b] Regal Size[/b] and amazing boost from [b]conversions[/b]. One other glyph you can consider taking to the endgame is [b]Cyddstep[/b], which will let you build more corrosion and survive monster that kill you in a single hit. [b]Bysseps [/b]is average because you aren’t a striker (through it can help reduce resistances), [b]Halpmeh [/b]heals for less due to your lower base health, and [b]Weytwut [/b]is mainly used for mobility which you can get from Pisorf or the Bear Mace.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/aef0f769dad457ad85b4240b867c80aa2a9dcf78.png[/img]

[h2][b]Items[/b][/h2]
🧀 [b]Bear Mace and Whurrgarb[/b]l - More knockback and regen fighting synergies, yay! The Bear Mace makes your attacks knockback your targets, and much like with Pisorf, the Bear Mace will let the Rat deal its corrosion damage to both targets. What is different about the [b]Bear Mace[/b] is that the corrosion damage is triggered twice: once when you hit the enemy and a second time when they get knocked into the other enemy. [b]Whurrgarbl[/b] applies burning to enemies on hit. Burning makes monsters regenerate less health, which allows you to regen fight better and kill higher level enemies faster.

🧀 [b]Resistance items[/b] - As you’ll be taking lots of hits, items that reduce your damage taken are amazing. If you don’t want to prepare Bear Mace from the blacksmith, the [b]Shield [/b]is a great option. The Shield reduces your damage taken from attacks by 2. [b]Platemail [/b]is also a great find, as it reduces your damage taken by 2 per level at the cost of always attacking second. This is a great trade deal - perhaps the greatest in the history of trade deals - as we don’t mind attacking second because we’re finishing with [b]Burndayraz[/b] anyways!.

Some other top purchase worth mentioning are the [b]Venom Dagge[/b]r to help with regen fighting, the [b]Elven Boots[/b] to boost your mana for spells and Magic Resistance, and finally the [b]Bloody Sigil [/b]to keep you healthy. Happy shopping!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/d61e0ebd5dce8247f786313cc82529cd6763c7a5.png[/img]

[h2][b]Combos[/b][/h2]
🧀 [b]Flambé [/b]- Corrode a couple times and then Fireball to finish (for anyone who likes their steaks well done.) If you want to fireball twice in a row, make sure to prepare Mana boosters!

🧀 [b]Marinate and Tenderise[/b] - Marinate a high health low damage enemy, like a Meat Man, then use them as a makeshift weapon. Make sure to not over tenderise while pushing them around like a bowling ball of death!

🧀 [b]Molecular Cooking[/b] - The hardest recipe and top combo that can help you double kill bosses at level one! Mix in damage reduction (or Cydstepp from your local store), Burndayraz, and plenty of Corrosion to prepare. Build up that signature corrosive flavour, tenderise and flambe, then finish with 20 minutes in the Pisorf oven. Add Imawal to taste.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/946512227c49217e4f0fdb745cabb1ae21d74dec.gif[/img]

And that's it for today's class post! If you want to be the Rat Monarch destined to build their empire, make sure to wishlist Desktop Dungeons: Rewind!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1976950/Desktop_Dungeons_Rewind/

Also be sure to follow QCF Design on Twitter for more Desktop Dungeons: Rewind content: https://twitter.com/QCFdesign

notes.title: The Warlord - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #5
notes.content:
In the spirit of the season, we’re going to be looking at our favourite Desktop Dungeons class with death protection: the Warlords. They are the best users of [b]Cydstepp[/b], a high cost glyph which allows the caster to survive a hit that would otherwise kill them. Warlords ride on the edge of life and death to show their foes that they aren’t going down without a fight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/96e7881c53ab2382cd1ef84d1e128752e7d249d2.png[/img]

I’ve gotten a Warlord to do this class breakdown, but I must warn you, they seem to have gotten into New Year’s Resolutions a little early and… Have become a little obsessed with exercise. 

Without further ado, I introduce the Warlord!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/ab423e69bf6d7d6c49637f6741436d48d6addfd1.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Abilities[/b][/h2]
🏋️‍♀️ [b]Courageous [/b]– Drinking a Mana Potion will cause the next attack to do +30% damage
🏋️‍♀️ [b]Determined [/b]– +30% bonus damage whenever below half health
🏋️‍♀️ [b]Defiant [/b]– Starts with the CYDSTEPP glyph, always castable

Warlords have found a way to be the strongest and most well-rounded Striker class in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind, and that is HIMT (High Instensity Mortality Training.) While most Strikers find joy in exercising their weapon swinging abilities and then recovering before continuing to fight, Warlords push themselves to the brink of collapse in a short amount of time. Remember, if you aren’t vomiting, you aren’t doing it right!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/3fd4bf7bb0d9713848082a75c745ed2718171442.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Kin Choices[/b][/h2]
🏋️‍♀️ [b]Gnomes [/b]– Gnomes are our WOD (Warlord of the Day.) Their ability to create Mana Potions synergises with the Warlord’s [b]Courageous [/b]trait, while also giving them enough mana to [b]Cydstepp [/b]permanent death or severe injury once more! Mana potions are also very hydrating and one of the easiest drinks to keep down!
🏋️‍♀️ [b]Orcs [/b]– We’re not about numbers around here. We’re about functional monster un-aliving ability! But the Orc has… Numbers that we simply can’t ignore. The Orc’s conversion bonus of +2 base damage synergises incredibly well with the [b]Determined [/b]and [b]Courageous [/b]traits. Now that’s functional!
🏋️‍♀️ [b]Elves [/b]– The true masters of AMCAP (As Many Cydtepps as Possible)! When combined with the ways of [b]Mystera[/b], whose machinations are unknown and unknowable, their bonus mana from conversions can help Warlords use [b]Cydstepp 3 times[/b] in a session! Now that’ll keep you going!

As a side note,[i] you too[/i] can become a Warlord! Almost all the kin in Desktop Dungeons have tried it a couple times and come out functionally fitter than before, [b]Dwarves[/b] and [b]Humans [/b]in particular. Don’t let the stereotypes hold you back, we’re very accepting and not insane at all!!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/98f92c5e562369e44f4b49e10e93fe498047f663.png[/img]

[h2][b]Gods[/b][/h2]
🏋️‍♂️ [b]Mystera Annur[/b]– The God that other Strikers won’t listen to. “You need to be sensible!” they say, “Worship Taurog or Earthmother, it’s healthier.” Some of them even claim that “[i]20% of Warlords end up with serious physical injuries.[/i]” They’re wrong. Mystera helps Warlords turn their habit of being near death into piety, and that piety into being near death more often. Doesn’t that sound perfect! [b]Mystic Balance[/b] makes Cydstepp cost less, [b]Magic[/b] increases your mana, and [b]Refreshment [/b]can keep you going for just a bit longer.
🏋️‍♂️ [b]Jehora Jeheyu[/b] – Some say Mystera's advice is weird and harming our health… I can’t wait to hear what they say about Jehora. So what you’re weakened, poisoned, corroded, and mana burned? Gonna cry?? [b]Boost Health[/b] and [b]Boost Mana[/b] can help Warlords stay low without dying and cast more Cydstepps! Jehora Jeheyu really is the most generous and unknowable cosmic horror.
🏋️‍♂️ [b]Glowing Guardian[/b] – We don’t need too much training equipment, and Mr. GG agrees! While he’s not our first choice of trainer, [b]Humility [/b]gives us more experience, [b]Consecrated Strike[/b] can help crack through physical resistances, and [b]Absolution [/b]helps us stay up a little longer! Though he’s against us drinking our uhh… Potions. So we don’t stick around too long.

While these are the best places for Warlords to worship, any box will do! [b]Earthmothe[/b]r is onto something with her diet plans, [b]Binlor [/b]builds our resistances, and [b]Pacty [/b]supports quietly. Anything but [b]Tikki Tooki[/b] or [b]Taurog[/b]! Warlords want to get hit, and Tikki doesn’t like that… Really good Warlords can work out around this, but it’s not recommended for beginners. Taurog doesn't like casting spells, which can make using Cydstepp difficult without being punished.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/fcc06f3044855c4a96e93762efcfd77e0a0c74f8.png[/img]

[h2][b]Glyphs[/b][/h2]
🏋️‍♂️ [b]Cydstepp [/b]– The bread and butter (proverbially, we don’t eat those) of the Warlord way! Defiant allows Warlords to cast this Glyphs while below 50% HP, letting them to chain attacks together while on the edge of mortality with the Determined trait active the entire time. You’ll be using most of your mana on this Glyph, so make sure to always precast it before exploring!
🏋️‍♂️ [b]Imawal [/b]– Damn right I am! Warlords tend to punch above their weight to an unreasonable degree, and so Imawal’s Bonus Experience can become a great gateway to functional high level monster slaying.
🏋️‍♂️ [b]Getindare [/b]– When the last hit will kill you, hit them first! When combining Getindare with Cydstepp Warlord can pull off some nasty combos. You string of exercises will look something like this: attack once to get below half health and activate [b]Determined[/b], then attack again to break [b]Death Protection[/b], finally cast [b]Cydstepp [/b]and attack again. At this point, you won’t have enough mana to Cydstepp death, but a swift blow to their skull with [b]Getindare [/b]might just do the job to floor them before they floor you!

As it is with all Strikers, [b]Bysseps [/b]is also good. We know the Barbarians are fighting over if it’s right to use Bysseps or not, claiming it might be unhealthy, but Mystera tells us it’s perfectly safe! And we trust Mystera above all. You probably won’t be holding onto [b]Burndayraz [/b]for too long because you’ll be spending your mana on [b]Cydstepp[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/b603f5236abd005db144daf595b2668029feadca.png[/img]

Well, what are you waiting for!? Use all of that high intensity energy to smash that wishlist button so you can be functionally fit with all of your new Warlord friends!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1976950/Desktop_Dungeons_Rewind/

Also be sure to follow QCF Design on Twitter for more Desktop Dungeons: Rewind content: https://twitter.com/QCFdesign

notes.title: The Berserker - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #4
notes.content:
[h2]THE BERSERKER IS THE STRONGEST AND BESTEST CLASS IN ALL OF DESKTOP DUNGEONS, THEY HAVE NO WEAKNESSES WHATSOEVER AND ARE VERY GOOD AT TURNING ENEMIES INTO ENEMY 
COLOURED SMEARS DUNGEON FLOOR![/h2]

Alright Berserker, lets calm down a bit and look at the intricate complicated ways this class can pulverize any who oppose them and... Oh wait you'd prefer if the Berserker takes over this episode? 

Yes? Really?

Fine, take it away...

[h1]YES! BERSERKER WILL START BY SHOWING OFF WHAT BERSERKER CAN DO![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/b28751e29ec51a191e908b50ced08f399233c6c5.gif[/img]

[h2][b]ABILITIES [/b][/h2]

notes.title: The Thief - Exploring character classes in Desktop Dungeons: Rewind #3
notes.content:
The thief is one of the first unlockable classes, as well as being one of the best pickups for the early dungeons. They synergize well with humans and orcs early on in the game and have high adaptability that comes from their Hoarder trait. They can find more boosters, glyphs, and shops to play around while conserving tiles.

Let's check out their bonuses:
[list]
[*] Stabber - Deals an extra 30% damage to enemies with full health
[*] Hoarder - +33% more items on the dungeon map
[*] Survivor - All Health Potions and Mana Potions restore both health and mana
[/list]
The Stabber trait also allows them to become incredibly powerful with levels as the percentage damage increase scales. Having more potions in the Dungeon due to the Hoarder trait and makes the Survivor trait even stronger as all potions restore both health and mana!

But wait! There are even more cool tricks up the Thief's thieving sleeves.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/1388034ee3c8f65cc427eb0335f37860557c4aef.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Glyph Usage[/b][/h2]

[h3][i]Bysseps[/i][/h3]
💎Thieves are great users of Bysseps: make your first attack hit even harder, adding percentage scaling on top of percentage scaling like an aggressive lasagne!
💎If you can tank a single hit from a higher-level enemy, combine this with Getindare and you have an amazing 2 shot combo which looks a little bit like this -  Bysseps > attack > Bysseps > Getindare > attack and kill.

[h3][i]Pisorf[/i][/h3]
💎Pisorf spamming can be particularly strong if you're playing the Gnome (for mana potion refills) or Orc (for base damage scaling). 
💎This can be absolutely insane if you worship Binlor for a free Bysseps after a wall is destroyed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/6e987d7e539e2bbc8446f4bae34f48d18a67fbd6.png[/img]

[h2][b]God worship[/b][/h2]

[h3][i]Binlor Ironshield[/i][/h3]
💎If you're planning on spamming Pisorf, Binlor is always an amazing choice for farming piety and stacking resistance boons.
💎Stone Form can help you to stack bonus damage if you don't have Bysseps.
💎Stone Heart can be good for cracking through physical resists.

[h3][i]Earthmother[/i][/h3]
💎Scaling is important, and it's easier to scale when you have more HP. Vine Form is super good for this, and lets you get more value out of potions.
💎Entanglement can also help you to sneak in more hits against higher-level enemies, blasting you ahead in levels.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/1d36e83cced4ce5d6369dfadf54ccce9f91e887f.png[/img]

[h2][b]Kin matches[/b][/h2]

[h3][i]Damage Kin[/i][/h3]
💎Humans and Orcs can scale very hard with the Thief's Stabber bonus. With their conversions of +10% damage and +2 base damage, you can scale to the point where 2 shotting a monster 3 levels higher than you is possible.
💎In early game dungeons when scaling is easier, they are an amazing choice. However, in later dungeons, scaling to a point where you can roll enemies is not that easy, and Potion Kin becomes easier to win with.

[h3][i]Potion Kin[/i][/h3]
💎Gnomes and Halflings are both kin that creates potions with their conversions. Gnomes create mana potions, and Halflings create health potions.
💎The Rogue's Survivor ability allows them to use potions super effectively and can help them through the early game.
💎It is worth noting that potions restore their primary attribute by 40% and the secondary by 20% (health potions restore 40% of health and 20% of mana), so Halflings do better early game with leveling, and Gnomes do better late game with spell spamming.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42753242/e542254c3b864730321726727ecd516039acd7cb.png[/img]
